Subject: Kickoff: visibility & alerting work for Acme Health integration

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for taking this on. As we discussed in the vendor call, Acme Health needs a short, pragmatic visibility handoff so our SREs can operate the Redwood-powered inference endpoints in prod. Key asks from our side:

- A set of pre-built dashboards for latency, tail latency, token throughput, and cost-by-route.
- Tracing hooks (server span + model-inference span) and suggested span attributes (request_id, model_version, token_counts).
- An error taxonomy so we can route incidents (model-quality vs infra vs request-validation).
- Alert routing matrix and a first-pass runbook for P1/P2 (steps, on-call contact, escalation).

We attached our current infra diagram to help orient the plan (Acme-arch-diagram-v2.pdf).

Goal: have a consolidated runbook and dashboard bundle ready for a review on 2027-09-09.

Please loop in whoever from Redwood ops should own the tech details; Tim O'Riley (cc) will be the Acme on-call contact for this project.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Mills

Acme Health

4) Alert routing + runbooks: CSV routing matrix, MD runbook template for P1/P2/P3 with clear triage steps and playbook links.

Subject: Re: Kickoff: visibility & alerting work for Acme Health integration

Hi all — technical note attached below (short summary first). I drafted recommended span names and minimal annotations that Acme engineers can add to their gateway and inference client wrappers.

Summary of concrete items I added to the Drive doc (link below):
- Span plan: HTTP server span -> Redwood-request span -> Model-inference span. Add attributes: request_id, user_id (hashed), model_family, model_version, prompt_length, response_length, tokens_charged.
- Trace sampling: adaptive sampling at 1% overall with a head-sampled set for any request above 500ms or error status.
- Metrics: per-route token_in, token_out, generation_latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), kv-cache-hit-rate.
- Error taxonomy draft:
  * ModelQuality: hallucination, content_error (owner: App), score_threshold_breach (owner: ML)
  * InferenceInfra: oom, gpu_failure, container_restart (owner: Infra)
  * ClientInput: malformed_request, rate_limit_exceeded (owner: App)
- Alerting guidance:
  P1 (sev1): service-wide cold-start or >50% error rate for 10m -> page Infra on-call
  P2: model-quality regressions above threshold -> page ML + CS to coordinate rollback
  P3: degraded metrics below thresholds (p95 increase) -> slack notify, create ticket

JIRA ticket OPS-4782 created to track the work (please add ACs). I put a draft dashboards.json (Grafana) in the Drive folder and a short example on how to add the model_version variable to each panel.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/AcmeHealth/visibility-specs

Attachment: (embedding snippets and the suggested YAML for sampling) — small code sample included inline.

Laura Bennett
Principal Instrumentation Engineer
Redwood Inference
